author: ABC-Belarus
title: The reality of released Belarusian anarchist prisoners: Why our support doesn’t stop at prison doorstep
content:
In the last two years, quite a few of our comrades left prison: some after completing their sentences, others were released as a result of pardons negotiated between the dictator and US diplomats in exchange of easing sanctions. We are preparing a longer analysis on this kind of trading and how it enables dictatorship, but today, we wanted to focus on what awaits released political prisoners on the outside and why they need even more support than before.

As a reminder, all imprisoned anarchists are put on a list of extremists and some additionally end up on the terrorist list. What is means is that once they are released in Belarus, they can’t open a bank account, can’t register a phone number, can’t register as self-employed. Of course, most employers would refuse hiring them as they can’t even transfer salary to the ex-prisoner, saying nothing of them being scared of engaging with an “extremist”. People on the extremist list can’t engage in publishing activity or teaching. Combined, this effectively pushes the released to the grey economy zone and makes them dependent on external support.
